reply.title: At the Highest Point
reply.story: You toss a tennis ball straight up into the air. As it climbs, it slows down until it hangs suspended for a single, motionless instant at its peak before falling back into your hand. It is easy to watch the ball stop and wonder: if its speed drops to zero at the top, does its acceleration also vanish for that brief moment? Galileo wrestled with how things speed up and slow down, realizing that gravity does not switch off just because a moving object pauses. Let us trace the motion from launch to return and see what happens to velocity and acceleration at the very top.
reply.cardDescription: Explore a ball thrown straight up. See how velocity changes while acceleration stays constant at $-gravity$, even when the ball stops at the top.
reply.instructions: Adjust the launch speed and press Play to watch the motion. Use the scrubber or At Top button to inspect the peak.

words.motion_top: At the top for an instant
